facts.statement: The genus Zby contains only one known species, Zby atlanticus.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Zby atlanticus.

facts.statement: The fossils of Zby were discovered in 1996 in the Lourinhã Formation of Portugal by Octávio Mateus.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 1996 in the Lourinhã Formation, Portugal by Octávio Mateus.

facts.statement: Zby was first described and named by Octávio Mateus, Philip D. Mannion, and Paul Upchurch in 2014.
facts.quote: Zby was first described and named by Octávio Mateus, Philip D. Mannion and Paul Upchurch in 2014

facts.statement: Zby is estimated to have been between 15 and 18 meters long.
facts.quote: Zby is estimated to measure around 15 to 18 metres in length.

facts.statement: Zby is distinguished from other sauropods by four unique features, including a prominent ridge on the humerus near the deltopectoral crest.
facts.quote: Zby is differentiated from other sauropods based on four autapomorphies, including a prominent posteriorly projecting ridge on the humerus at the level of the deltopectoral crest.

facts.statement: Most anatomical features indicate that Zby was a non-neosauropod eusauropod belonging to the Turiasauria group.
facts.quote: Nearly all other anatomical features suggest that Zby is a non-neosauropod eusauropod, confirming its position as a turiasaurian.

facts.statement: Zby is classified within the unranked family Turiasauria.
Zby lived during the late Jurassic period, between 155 and 150 million years ago in the Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, entre 155 y 150 millones de años durante el Kimmeridgiense

facts.statement: The time range for Zby is the Kimmeridgian stage, from 152.21 to 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is noted that Zby was initially thought to be the species Turiasaurus riodevensis before being reclassified.
facts.quote: although it was initially thought to be Turiasaurus riodevensis.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Zby is closely related to Turiasaurus riodevensis from contemporaneous deposits in eastern Spain.
facts.quote: Se ha sugerido que Zby está emparentado de cerca con Turiasaurus riodevensis que proviene de depósitos aproximadamente contemporáneos en el este de España

rejected.statement: Zby is an extinct genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur found in the Late Jurassic Lourinhã Formation of central west Portugal.
rejected.quote: Zby is an extinct genus of turiasaurian sauropod dinosaur known from the Late Jurassic, particularly late Kimmeridgian stage of the Lourinhã Formation, in central west Portugal.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Zby is an extinct genus of turiasaurian sauropod'

rejected.statement: Zby is known only from a holotype consisting of a partial skeleton with a complete tooth, a cervical neural arch fragment, an anterior chevron, and an almost complete right pectoral girdle and forelimb.
rejected.quote: Zby is known solely from its holotype, a closely associated partial skeleton including a complete tooth with root, a fragment of cervical neural arch, an anterior chevron, and an almost complete right pectoral girdle and forelimb.
